subject: Decision Making
title: Self-Driving Car Dilemmas
description: A micro-lesson that makes Self-Driving Car Dilemmas usable.

hook.text: A self-driving car must choose: hit five pedestrians or swerve and kill the single passenger.

buildup.text: Self-Driving Car Dilemmas sets up the tradeoffs, the uncertainty, and the decision pressure.

discovery.text: People want cars that protect pedestrians in surveys. But they want to buy cars that protect the passenger. A paradox.

twist.text: In practice, self-driving cars avoid the dilemma by braking and minimizing impact.

climax.text: Self-driving cars force us to program morality explicitly. Humans react intuitively.

punchline.text: Save passengers or pedestrians? Algorithms need moral rules humans never had to.

quiz.question: What paradox did the Moral Machine reveal?
options: People want cars that save pedestrians but buy cars that protect passengers
